learn.hook: You cannot see it, but you are carrying a blanket of air above you that reaches hundreds of kilometres into space. It even keeps meteors from hitting you!
points: The atmosphere is the layer of air held around the Earth by gravity. Dry air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen; argon, carbon dioxide and other gases make up the remaining 1% or so. Water vapour and dust are also present in varying amounts.
Troposphere (lowest, about 13 km on average; higher at the equator, lower at the poles): almost all weather, clouds and water vapour are here, and temperature falls as you go up.
Stratosphere (up to about 50 km): contains the ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays from the Sun. It has almost no clouds, so its lower part is good for flying aeroplanes.
Mesosphere (up to about 80 km): the coldest layer; meteors burn up here and look like shooting stars.
Thermosphere (about 80 to 400 km) contains the ionosphere, which reflects radio waves back to the Earth. Above it is the exosphere, where the air is extremely thin.

example.q: Think it through: A pilot flying from Delhi to Kolkata climbs above the clouds and the ride becomes smooth. Which layer is the plane in, and why is it calm?
steps: Clouds, rain, storms and most bumpy air movements happen in the troposphere.
Above the troposphere is the stratosphere, which has almost no clouds or weather.
So when the plane rises above the weather into the lower stratosphere, the air is steady.
example.answer: In the lower stratosphere, which is above the clouds and weather of the troposphere.

learn.reallife: Doctors advise sunscreen because some UV rays still reach us; the ozone layer stops most of them. The radio you hear and the shooting stars you see on clear nights both depend on layers of the atmosphere.

games.title: Air facts: true or false?
items: Nitrogen is the most plentiful gas in the air.
Nitrogen makes up about 78% of dry air.
The ozone layer is found in the troposphere.
The ozone layer is in the stratosphere.
Almost all weather happens in the troposphere.
Clouds, rain and storms form in the lowest layer, where most water vapour is.
Meteors burn up in the mesosphere.
Friction with the air in the mesosphere burns most meteors, making shooting stars.
Radio waves are reflected back to Earth by the stratosphere.
The ionosphere, part of the thermosphere, reflects radio waves.
The troposphere is thicker over the equator than over the poles.
It reaches about 18 km at the equator but only about 8 km at the poles.

quiz.q: About what percentage of dry air is nitrogen?
quiz.explain: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of dry air, oxygen about 21% and the other gases together about 1%.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the share of nitrogen with that of oxygen

items: Nitrogen
Oxygen
Others

quiz.q: In which layer do clouds, rain and storms mostly form?
quiz.explain: The troposphere holds almost all the water vapour and dust, so weather happens there.
quiz.mistake: Thinks weather happens high up in the sky in the upper layers

quiz.q: The ozone layer protects us by absorbing:
quiz.explain: Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what kind of radiation ozone blocks

quiz.q: Shooting stars are meteors burning up in which layer?
quiz.explain: Most meteors burn up in the mesosphere, about 50 to 80 km above the Earth.
quiz.mistake: Thinks meteors burn up near the ground or in the ozone layer

quiz.q: Which part of the atmosphere reflects radio waves back to the Earth?
quiz.explain: The ionosphere, within the thermosphere, has charged particles that bounce radio waves back to the Earth.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the ionosphere with the ozone layer

quiz.q: What generally happens to temperature as you go higher in the troposphere?
quiz.explain: Air in the troposphere is heated mainly from the ground, so it gets colder with height. That is why hill stations are cool.
quiz.mistake: Thinks being closer to the Sun makes high places hotter

quiz.q: Why is the lower stratosphere suitable for flying aeroplanes?
options: It is closest to the ground
It has almost no clouds or weather disturbances
quiz.explain: Above the troposphere there are hardly any clouds or storms, so flights are smoother.
quiz.mistake: Thinks planes need more oxygen or warmth rather than calm air

quiz.q: What holds the atmosphere around the Earth?
quiz.explain: The Earth's gravity pulls the gases of the atmosphere towards it, so they do not escape into space.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the ozone layer acts like a lid holding the air in

teach.ask: Gappu flaps upwards: "If I keep flying up and up, what will I pass through in the sky?"
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! Troposphere with weather, stratosphere with ozone, mesosphere with burning meteors, then the thermosphere and exosphere. I will stay in the troposphere, thank you!
teach.nudge: Nice! But what comes after the layer with clouds, and where is the ozone that protects me?

learn.hook: "Carry an umbrella today" is about weather. "Mumbai is warm and humid" is about climate. Can you spot the difference?
points: Weather is the state of the atmosphere at a place for a short time, like a few hours or a day. It can change quickly.
Climate is the average weather of a place over a long period, usually about 30 years or more.
The elements of weather and climate are temperature, air pressure, wind, humidity (water vapour in the air) and precipitation (rain, snow, hail).
Air pressure is highest at sea level and falls with height. Wind blows from areas of high pressure to areas of low pressure.

Instruments: thermometer (temperature), barometer (air pressure), anemometer (wind speed), wind vane (wind direction), rain gauge (rainfall) and hygrometer (humidity). The India Meteorological Department (IMD) records weather and issues forecasts.

example.q: Think it through: On a day in Chennai, the morning is sunny, the afternoon has a thunderstorm and the night is cool. Does Chennai's climate change three times that day?
steps: The sunny morning, stormy afternoon and cool night are changes in weather, which can change within hours.
Climate is the average pattern of many years, so one day cannot change it.
Chennai's climate stays the same: warm and humid for most of the year.
example.answer: No. Only the weather changed; climate is the long-term average and does not change in a day.

learn.reallife: Farmers watch the weather forecast before sowing or spraying crops, while builders and planners use climate data to design houses and drains.

quiz.q: Which statement describes climate rather than weather?
options: Kerala receives heavy rain every monsoon season
It is cloudy in Pune right now
Tomorrow will be windy in Goa
quiz.explain: Climate is the usual pattern over many years. The other statements describe conditions for a short time.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any statement about rain or wind is about climate

quiz.q: Climate is usually worked out from weather records of about how many years or more?
quiz.explain: Climate is the average of weather over a long period, usually about 30 years or more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a single year or a few years of records is enough to describe climate

quiz.q: Which instrument measures air pressure?
quiz.explain: A barometer measures air pressure. A falling barometer reading often warns of stormy weather.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of weather instruments

quiz.q: An anemometer is used to measure:
quiz.explain: The spinning cups of an anemometer turn faster in stronger wind. Wind direction is shown by a wind vane.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the anemometer with the wind vane

quiz.q: Wind blows from:
options: low pressure areas to high pressure areas
high pressure areas to low pressure areas
the poles only to the deserts
quiz.explain: Air moves from where pressure is higher to where it is lower, just like air rushing out of a pumped-up balloon.
quiz.mistake: Reverses the direction of air movement

quiz.q: Humidity means:
options: the amount of dust in the air
the amount of water vapour in the air
quiz.explain: Humidity tells us how much water vapour the air holds. High humidity makes us feel sticky, as in coastal cities.
quiz.mistake: Confuses humidity with air pressure or rainfall

quiz.q: Where is air pressure highest?
options: On the top of Mount Everest
In the middle of the stratosphere
quiz.explain: At sea level there is the most air pressing down from above, so pressure is highest. It falls as we go up.
quiz.mistake: Thinks pressure increases with height

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT an element of weather?
quiz.explain: Temperature, air pressure, wind, humidity and precipitation are the elements of weather. Soil is part of the land, not the atmosphere.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which features belong to the atmosphere

teach.ask: Gappu says: "It rained today, so my city now has a rainy climate! Am I right?"
teach.praise: Tweet! One rainy day is weather. Climate is the average of many years of temperature, rain and wind. Now I get it!
teach.nudge: Hmm, so what is the difference in time between weather and climate?

learn.hook: Shimla and Ludhiana are only about 130 km apart as the crow flies, yet in May one is pleasant and the other is baking. Why?
points: Latitude: places near the equator get more direct sunlight and are hot; places towards the poles are cooler. The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of India.
Altitude: temperature in the troposphere falls by about 6.5 °C for every 1,000 m of height, so hill stations like Shimla, Ooty and Darjeeling are cool.
Distance from the sea: the sea keeps coastal places like Mumbai and Chennai moderate (equable). Places far inland like Delhi have extreme (continental) climates with hot summers and cold winters.

Relief and winds: the Himalayas block cold winds from Central Asia and make the monsoon winds shed their rain over India. Windward slopes of mountains get heavy rain; the leeward side stays drier (rain shadow).
Ocean currents also matter: warm currents warm nearby coasts, cold currents cool them. India has a monsoon type of climate; the south-west monsoon usually reaches Kerala around 1 June.

example.q: Think it through: A town at the foot of a hill is at 30 °C. What will be the temperature at a hill station 2,000 m higher, using the normal lapse rate?
steps: Temperature falls by about 6.5 °C for every 1,000 m.
2,000 m is 2 × 1,000 m, so the fall is 2 × 6.5 = 13 °C.

learn.reallife: Families from the plains go to Nainital or Munnar in summer to escape the heat, thanks to altitude. Weather apps in Mumbai rarely show the extreme heat that Delhi sees, thanks to the sea.

Which place in Meghalaya gets the highest average rainfall in the world?
The hot, dry summer wind of north India is called?

Is Mumbai's climate equable or extreme?

quiz.q: Ooty is much cooler than Chennai in summer mainly because of its:
quiz.explain: Ooty is high up in the Nilgiri Hills. Temperature falls with height, so it is cooler.
quiz.mistake: Thinks latitude explains every temperature difference

quiz.q: A place at sea level has a temperature of 30 °C. Using a fall of 6.5 °C per 1,000 m, what is the temperature at 2,000 m (in °C)?
quiz.explain: The fall is 2 × 6.5 = 13 °C, so the temperature is 30 − 13 = 17 °C.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts only one step of 6.5, gives the fall instead of the temperature, or adds instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Why does Delhi have hotter summers and colder winters than Mumbai?
options: Delhi is closer to the equator
Delhi is at a much higher altitude
Delhi is far from the moderating effect of the sea
quiz.explain: The sea heats and cools slowly and keeps Mumbai's temperatures moderate. Delhi, far inland, has an extreme climate.
quiz.mistake: Does not know about the effect of distance from the sea

quiz.q: How do the Himalayas affect India's climate?
options: They bring cold winds into the plains
They block cold Central Asian winds and help the monsoon winds bring rain to India
They stop all rain from reaching India
They make the sea warmer near Kerala
quiz.explain: The Himalayas act as a wall: they keep out icy winds in winter and trap the monsoon winds so they rain over India.
quiz.mistake: Thinks mountains only make places colder

quiz.q: Which place is known for receiving the highest average rainfall in the world?
quiz.explain: Mawsynram in Meghalaya, in the Khasi Hills, receives the highest average rainfall in the world.
quiz.mistake: Confuses very wet places with very dry ones like Jaisalmer and Leh

quiz.q: The leeward side of a mountain range usually:
options: gets less rain and is called a rain shadow area
quiz.explain: Moist winds drop most rain on the windward side as they rise. Air coming down the far side is drier.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the windward and leeward sides

quiz.q: The south-west monsoon normally arrives in Kerala around:
quiz.explain: The usual onset date of the south-west monsoon over Kerala is around 1 June, and it then spreads across India.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the season of the south-west monsoon

quiz.q: Which latitude line passes through the middle of India?
quiz.explain: The Tropic of Cancer (23°30′ N) divides India into a southern tropical part and a northern subtropical part. Mainland India lies roughly between 8° N and 37° N.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Equator passes through India

teach.ask: Gappu is confused: "Why is it cool in Darjeeling and boiling in Delhi in May, when both are in north India?"
teach.praise: Squawk! Altitude, latitude, distance from the sea, mountains and winds all shape climate. Darjeeling is high up, so it stays cool!
teach.nudge: Good! But what difference does height make, and why are coastal cities less extreme?
